readout_other: electrooculography (EOG) recorded anti-saccade error rate and latency
direction_notes: Anti-saccade error rate fell with tFUS (about -10 %p in S1 and -16 %p in S2) with no significant change in latency; the authors interpret this as enhanced DLPFC-mediated inhibitory signalling from an excitatory effect.
safety_notes: Simulation-based acoustic and thermal safety assessment (temperature rise below 0.05 C); neither subject heard any sound or reported neurological or psychological side effects.

timing.protocol_description: tFUS to the left DLPFC was randomly applied once in every set of four anti-saccade trials, starting 200 ms before saccade target onset and lasting 500 ms; no consecutive stimulation trials.

source_quotes.n_subjects: While human participants (n 2) were performing AS tasks, tFUS stimulations were randomly applied to the left DLPFC right after the fixation target disappeared.
